name: Ruff
tagline: A Python linter and formatter whose Rust workspace also contains the ty type checker.
hook: A Rust workspace guide to environment traps, Markdown tests, ty-specific work, security reviews, and focused references.
summary: Ruff covers its Rust workspace and adds a focused section for ty. The guide explains environment traps, treats Markdown tests as readable specifications, and points security reviews and specialized ty work to separate documents.

techniques.title: Explain the hidden configuration behind a reproduction
techniques.body: Keep temporary Python files outside the checkout because configuration discovery changes their inferred Python version. The rule names the controlling key and the wrong in-repository default.
techniques.quote: A file inside the checkout discovers Ruff's root `pyproject.toml`, whose `requires-python = ">=3.7"` causes ty to infer Python 3.7 as the default Python version.

techniques.title: Separate review findings from agent workflow rules
techniques.body: Review should report introduced code, test, and architectural violations. The file explicitly excludes unrelated existing issues and warns against treating agent-only workflow requirements as obligations on human PR authors.
techniques.quote:
Report
meaningful violations introduced by the changes; do not apply agent-only workflow
instructions to PR authors or flag unrelated pre-existing issues.

techniques.title: Give generated snapshots a single update path
techniques.body: Snapshot-update environment variables are supplied for both nextest and cargo test. Agents must inspect the resulting diffs and pending inline snapshots instead of manually changing expected output.
techniques.quote: Never edit snapshot files or inline snapshot bodies manually. Regenerate them by running the relevant tests with the snapshot-update environment variables documented above, then review the generated diff.

techniques.title: Route security reviews to the relevant threat model
techniques.body: Runtime changes and repository, CI, or release changes use different threat-model documents. The routing gives severity assessment a stated trust boundary instead of relying on a generic security checklist.
techniques.quote:
For security reviews of repository, CI, and release changes, use the
[repository threat model](agents/references/repository-threat-model.md) to assess
trust boundaries and calibrate severity.

techniques.title: Write for someone outside the current session
techniques.body: Public text should explain the final observable behavior and verified evidence. Before finishing, the agent rereads each artifact without assuming the reader has access to the coding conversation.
techniques.quote: Before finishing, reread each changed artifact as someone with no access to the Codex session and remove or explain anything that would surprise or confuse that reader.

steal: Document configuration-discovery traps beside reproduction instructions.
State which workflow rules apply to agents rather than all contributors.
Provide the regeneration command and require review of its output.
Route security work by the trust boundary it touches.
